title: AIIMS NORCET FON Pattern Mock Test (70 Questions) — Infection Control, Hand Hygiene, PPE, CSSD & BMW
description: 70-question AIIMS NORCET scenario-based & PYQ test covering Infection Control & Isolation Precautions, WHO Hand Hygiene Standards, PPE Donning & Doffing, Sterilization & CSSD, and India BMW Rules (2016 & 2018) with +1/-0.33 marking, MSQs, hints, and rationales.
subject: norcet-fon
topic: Infection Control, Hand Hygiene, PPE, CSSD & BMW Management
instructions: AIIMS NORCET Exam Pattern — Fundamentals of Nursing (70 Questions / 70 Minutes)
Sections: Infection Control (14Q), Hand Hygiene WHO (14Q), PPE Donning & Doffing (14Q), Sterilization & CSSD (14Q), BMW Management (14Q)
Marking Scheme: +1 mark per correct response | -0.33 negative mark per wrong attempt | 0 for skipped
Hint Coins: 4 Hint Coins credited (5% of 70 questions) — hints stay disabled until clicked

questions.question: A patient is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis and a productive cough. Which isolation precautions and room specifications are required by the nurse?

options.text: Droplet precautions in a positive-pressure room with a surgical mask
Airborne precautions in a negative-pressure Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) with an N95 respirator
Contact precautions in a shared ward with gloves and gown only
Standard precautions only with bed curtains drawn

questions.explanation: [NORCET-11 Mains PYQ] Pulmonary tuberculosis spreads via airborne droplet nuclei (< 5 microns) that remain suspended in air. It requires Airborne precautions: a negative-pressure AIIR (at least 12 air changes/hour for new facilities), door kept closed, and a fit-tested N95 respirator for staff.
questions.hint: Consider the particle size of TB bacilli and which room airflow direction prevents contaminated air from escaping into the hallway.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: Which of the following diseases require AIRBORNE precautions in addition to Standard Precautions? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Pulmonary tuberculosis
Measles (Rubeola)
Varicella (Chickenpox)
Pertussis (Whooping cough)

questions.explanation: The classic triad for Airborne precautions is "MTV": Measles, Tuberculosis, and Varicella (plus disseminated herpes zoster). Pertussis spreads via large respiratory droplets (> 5 microns) and requires Droplet precautions.
questions.hint: Recall the high-yield three-letter mnemonic "MTV" for pathogens transmitted via tiny suspended droplet nuclei.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A patient with confirmed Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection has frequent watery diarrhea. Which isolation precaution and hand hygiene agent are mandatory?

options.text: Droplet precautions and 70% alcohol hand rub
Contact precautions (gown and gloves) and handwashing with soap and water
Airborne precautions and N95 respirator
Protective isolation and sterile surgical gloves

questions.explanation: C. difficile spreads via fecal-oral contact and produces hardy bacterial spores that are resistant to alcohol-based hand rubs. Contact precautions (gown + gloves) and mechanical handwashing with soap and water are mandatory.
questions.hint: Think about how bacterial spores respond to alcohol rub versus mechanical friction with running water.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A nurse is caring for a patient with Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcal meningitis). Within what distance from the patient must the nurse wear a surgical mask under Droplet precautions?

options.text: Within 1 foot (0.3 meters)
Within 3 feet (1 meter)
Only when performing endotracheal intubation
Only when standing outside the closed door

questions.explanation: Respiratory droplets (> 5 microns) travel short distances through the air when coughing, sneezing, or talking—typically up to 3 feet (1 meter). A surgical mask is required whenever entering the room or working within 3 feet of the patient.
questions.hint: Recall the standard horizontal travel radius of large respiratory droplets expelled during coughing.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: Which link in the Chain of Infection is broken when a nurse performs proper hand hygiene between two patients?

options.text: Infectious agent
Reservoir
Mode of transmission
Portal of entry

questions.explanation: The six links in the Chain of Infection are: Infectious agent -> Reservoir -> Portal of exit -> Mode of transmission -> Portal of entry -> Susceptible host. Hand hygiene interrupts the mode of transmission (direct/indirect contact transfer).
questions.hint: Identify which link represents the vehicle or pathway moving pathogens from one host to another.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A patient with severe neutropenia (ANC 300/mm3) following bone marrow transplantation is placed in Protective (Reverse) Isolation. Which room pressure and nursing precautions are required?

options.text: Negative-pressure room and fresh flowers at bedside for morale
Positive-pressure room with HEPA filtration, strict hand hygiene, and no fresh flowers or raw unwashed fruits
Shared room with another stable medical patient
Negative-pressure room with N95 mask for visitors only

questions.explanation: Protective (neutropenic) isolation shields an immunocompromised host from environmental pathogens. A positive-pressure HEPA-filtered room pushes air outward so outside pathogens cannot enter; fresh flowers, potted plants, and raw produce harbor Pseudomonas/Aspergillus and are prohibited.
questions.hint: Contrast keeping germs inside a room versus keeping outside germs from drifting toward an immunocompromised patient.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: Which healthcare-associated infection (HAI) is the MOST common worldwide, and what is the single most effective nursing measure to prevent it?

options.text: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP); routine antibiotic prophylaxis
Catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI); avoiding unnecessary catheterization and removing Foley catheters as soon as possible
Central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI); changing dressings weekly
Surgical site infection (SSI); shaving hair with a razor the night before surgery

questions.explanation: CAUTI accounts for the largest share of HAIs globally. The most effective prevention is minimizing catheter use and prompt removal (along with closed sterile drainage and keeping the bag below bladder level).
questions.hint: Think of the most frequently placed invasive device on hospital wards and the simplest way to eliminate its infection risk.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: While setting up a sterile field for a central line dressing change, which action by the nurse contaminates the sterile field?

options.text: Holding sterile objects above waist level
Keeping the sterile field within continuous visual sight
Reaching directly over the sterile field to pick up gauze from the far side
Treating the outer 1-inch (2.5 cm) border of the sterile drape as non-sterile

questions.explanation: Reaching over a sterile field risks shedding skin flora or droplets onto sterile items. Sterile objects must remain above waist level, in sight, and the outer 1-inch (2.5 cm) border is always considered unsterile.
questions.hint: Recall the core principle of surgical asepsis regarding body movement above an open sterile surface.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A nurse accidentally sustains a deep needle-stick injury from a hollow-bore needle just used on a patient with unknown HIV status. What is the nurse's IMMEDIATE first-aid action?

options.text: Squeeze the puncture site vigorously to force out blood and apply bleach
Wash the site immediately with soap and running water without squeezing or scrubbing harshly, then report for PEP evaluation
Ignore the injury unless the patient tests positive next week
Dip the finger into 2% glutaraldehyde solution

questions.explanation: Immediate management of needle-stick injury is gentle washing with soap and running water (do NOT squeeze/milk the wound or apply caustic antiseptics like bleach, which damage tissue and increase viral uptake), followed by immediate reporting and baseline testing/PEP within 2 hours (ideally, and up to 72 hours).
questions.hint: Remember what gentle first aid protects tissue integrity while flushing away surface blood.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: Which of the following infections require DROPLET precautions? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Influenza
Pertussis (Whooping cough)
Mumps and Rubella
Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) wound infection

questions.explanation: Droplet precautions apply to pathogens spread by large droplets (> 5 microns): Influenza, Pertussis, Mumps, Rubella, Diphtheria (pharyngeal), Meningococcal meningitis, and Mycoplasma pneumonia. MRSA wound infection requires Contact precautions.
questions.hint: Separate respiratory pathogens spread by large droplets from skin/wound organisms spread by direct touch.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A patient on Airborne precautions for active pulmonary TB must be transported to the radiology department for a chest X-ray. What is the nurse's priority infection control action?

options.text: Place an N95 respirator on the patient during transport
Place a standard surgical mask on the patient and notify radiology in advance
Cancel the chest X-ray permanently
Have the patient hold their breath in the elevator

questions.explanation: During transport, the patient wears a surgical mask (to contain expelled droplets/nuclei at the source; N95 masks are uncomfortable/unfitted for patients and valved N95s do not filter exhaled air), while transport staff wear N95 respirators if needed.
questions.hint: Think about source control for the patient versus respiratory protection for the staff member.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: Which element of the Chain of Infection does an indwelling Foley catheter or central venous catheter bypass?

options.text: Infectious agent
Reservoir
Portal of entry (intact skin and mucosal barriers)
Mode of transmission

questions.explanation: Invasive devices (catheters, IV lines, endotracheal tubes) bypass the body's natural anatomical defenses (skin and mucous membranes), creating a direct portal of entry for pathogens.
questions.hint: Consider which link represents the doorway through which microbes enter a host's body.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: A patient with localized herpes zoster (shingles) confined to a single thoracic dermatome can be managed with Standard precautions if lesions are completely covered. When must the nurse escalate to BOTH Airborne and Contact precautions?

options.text: Whenever the patient reports mild itching
When the lesions are disseminated (widespread) or the patient is immunocompromised
Only if the patient has a low-grade fever
Never; shingles only requires Droplet precautions

questions.explanation: Localized shingles in an immunocompetent host with covered lesions needs Standard precautions. Disseminated herpes zoster (or localized zoster in an immunocompromised host) sheds virus via both aerosols and vesicles, requiring Airborne + Contact precautions until all lesions crust over.
questions.hint: Think about when varicella-zoster virus stops staying localized and behaves like widespread chickenpox.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Standard Precautions must be applied to ALL patients in a healthcare facility regardless of their suspected or confirmed infection status.
Reason (R): Blood and body fluids of every patient are treated as potentially infectious for bloodborne and other transmissible pathogens.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Standard Precautions are the foundational tier of infection prevention applied universally to every patient because asymptomatic carriers may harbor bloodborne or transmissible pathogens without a known diagnosis.
questions.hint: Evaluate whether Standard Precautions depend on a confirmed lab diagnosis or apply universally to all blood and body fluids.
questions.subject: Infection Control & Isolation

questions.question: According to the WHO "My 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene," which sequence accurately represents all five moments?

options.text: Before entering hospital, before lunch, after charting, before shift change, after leaving ward
Before touching a patient, before clean/aseptic procedure, after body fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient, after touching patient surroundings
Before donning gown, before taking vitals, after taking vitals, before lunch, after restroom
Before medication prep, after medication prep, before dressing change, after dressing change, before discharge

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] The WHO 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene are: (1) Before touching a patient, (2) Before a clean/aseptic procedure, (3) After body fluid exposure risk, (4) After touching a patient, and (5) After touching patient surroundings.
questions.hint: Recall the exact two "Before" moments and three "After" moments defined by the World Health Organization.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: What is the WHO-recommended duration for performing hand hygiene using an Alcohol-Based Hand Rub (ABHR) versus washing hands with soap and water?

options.text: 5–10 seconds for ABHR; 15–20 seconds for soap and water
20–30 seconds for ABHR; 40–60 seconds for soap and water
60 seconds for ABHR; 20 seconds for soap and water
2 minutes for ABHR; 5 minutes for soap and water

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] WHO guidelines specify 20–30 seconds for rubbing hands with alcohol-based hand rub (until completely dry) and 40–60 seconds for the full handwashing procedure with soap and water.
questions.hint: Remember that soap-and-water washing takes roughly twice as long as alcohol hand rubbing.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: In which clinical situations MUST a nurse wash hands with soap and water rather than using an alcohol-based hand rub? (Select all that apply)

options.text: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
After caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) diarrhea
After using the restroom
Before measuring a routine blood pressure on an intact-skin patient when hands are visibly clean

questions.explanation: Soap and water is mandatory when hands are visibly dirty/soiled with proteinaceous material, after exposure to spore-forming pathogens (C. difficile, Bacillus anthracis) or norovirus, and after restroom use. When hands are visibly clean, ABHR is preferred for routine care.
questions.hint: Identify the situations where alcohol fails to penetrate dirt or kill hardy spores.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: A nurse adjusts the IV pump settings for a patient without directly touching the patient's skin, then leaves the bedside. Which WHO Moment for Hand Hygiene applies immediately afterward?

options.text: Moment 1: Before touching a patient
Moment 2: Before a clean/aseptic procedure
Moment 4: After touching a patient
Moment 5: After touching patient surroundings

questions.explanation: Touching any object or furniture in the patient's immediate zone (bed rails, IV pump, monitor, bedside table)—even without touching the patient directly—triggers WHO Moment 5 (After touching patient surroundings).
questions.hint: Notice that the nurse only touched equipment in the patient's immediate environment, not the patient's body.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: A nurse is about to insert a peripheral IV cannula into a patient's forearm after already greeting and assessing the patient's arm. Which WHO Moment for Hand Hygiene is required immediately before putting on gloves for the cannulation?

options.text: Moment 1: Before touching a patient
Moment 2: Before a clean/aseptic procedure
Moment 3: After body fluid exposure risk
Moment 5: After touching patient surroundings

questions.explanation: Moment 2 (Before clean/aseptic procedure) protects the patient from harmful germs—including their own skin flora—entering the body via an invasive site (IV cannulation, catheterization, wound dressing, suctioning).
questions.hint: Focus on protecting a vulnerable sterile entry site right before an invasive clinical task.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: What is the optimal concentration of alcohol (ethanol or isopropanol) in a WHO-recommended Alcohol-Based Hand Rub (ABHR) for maximum antimicrobial efficacy?

options.text: 60% to 80% (or up to 95%, typically 70–80% v/v)
100% absolute anhydrous alcohol

questions.explanation: Alcohol concentrations between 60% and 80% (WHO formulations use 80% ethanol or 75% isopropyl alcohol) are most effective because water is necessary to denature microbial proteins. Pure 100% alcohol evaporates too fast and coagulates surface proteins without penetrating cells.
questions.hint: Remember why a small amount of water is needed alongside alcohol to denature bacterial proteins effectively.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: According to WHO hand hygiene guidelines, how should a nurse position their hands while rinsing soap off during routine medical handwashing versus surgical hand scrubbing?

options.text: Hands pointed upward for medical handwashing; hands pointed downward for surgical scrubbing
Hands pointed downward (lower than elbows) for routine medical handwashing; hands pointed upward (higher than elbows) for surgical hand scrubbing
Hands kept strictly horizontal in both procedures
Direction of water flow does not matter in either procedure

questions.explanation: In routine medical handwashing, hands are kept lower than elbows so contaminated water drains down off the fingertips. In surgical scrubbing, hands are held higher than elbows so water runs from cleanest (fingertips) down toward least clean (elbows).
questions.hint: Apply the gravity rule: water should always flow from the cleanest area toward the dirtier area.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: Which area of the hands is MOST frequently missed during routine hand hygiene?

options.text: The center of the palms
Thumbs, fingertips, and spaces under the fingernails
The wrists
The forearms

questions.explanation: Observational studies and WHO training consistently show that thumbs (rotational rubbing), fingertips, and subungual spaces are the most commonly overlooked zones during handwashing and hand rubbing.
questions.hint: Think about the digits and tips that require dedicated rotational rubbing steps in the WHO technique.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: A nurse removes clean gloves after emptying a patient's urinary drainage bag. What is the nurse's NEXT mandatory action?

options.text: Proceed directly to the next patient because gloves protected the hands
Perform hand hygiene immediately (WHO Moment 3: After body fluid exposure risk)
Wipe the gloves with an alcohol swab and reuse them
Wash hands only if a visible tear is seen in the glove

questions.explanation: Wearing gloves NEVER replaces hand hygiene. Microscopic pinholes and hand contamination during glove removal occur frequently, making immediate hand hygiene mandatory after every glove removal.
questions.hint: Recall the golden rule regarding the relationship between glove use and hand hygiene.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: According to WHO and CDC standards for clinical nursing staff providing direct patient care, what is the rule regarding fingernails and jewelry?

options.text: Artificial gel nails are allowed if covered with clear polish
Natural fingernails must be kept short (< 0.5 cm or 1/4 inch), artificial nails are prohibited, and rings/watches/bracelets should be removed
Long nails are acceptable as long as gloves are worn
Rings with stones are permitted if washed with soap

questions.explanation: Artificial nails and long natural nails (> 0.5 cm / 1/4 inch) harbor Gram-negative bacilli and yeasts (e.g., Pseudomonas, Candida) and puncture gloves. Jewelry traps moisture and microbes and hinders thorough hand antisepsis.
questions.hint: Consider what harbors hidden pathogens and increases the risk of glove tears during clinical care.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: During a surgical hand scrub prior to an operation, what is the standard WHO-recommended duration using antimicrobial soap (e.g., 4% chlorhexidine gluconate or povidone-iodine)?

options.text: 20 to 30 seconds
40 to 60 seconds
2 to 5 minutes (typically 2–6 minutes per manufacturer/WHO protocol)
15 to 20 minutes

questions.explanation: WHO surgical hand preparation guidelines recommend scrubbing for 2–5 minutes (historically up to 6 minutes; prolonged 10-minute scrubs cause skin damage and increase bacterial shedding without extra efficacy).
questions.hint: Choose the duration longer than routine handwashing (40–60 sec) but short enough to avoid skin trauma.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: Which step of the WHO 6-step hand hygiene technique specifically cleans the dorsal (back) aspects of the fingers against the opposing palms?

options.text: Palm to palm
Right palm over left dorsum with interlaced fingers
Backs of fingers to opposing palms with fingers interlocked
Rotational rubbing of left thumb clasped in right palm

questions.explanation: Step 4 of the WHO hand hygiene technique ("backs of fingers to opposing palms with fingers interlocked") targets the knuckles and dorsal finger surfaces that palm-to-palm rubbing misses.
questions.hint: Visualize interlocking your fingers in a hook shape to rub the backs of your fingers against the opposite palm.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: Why should a nurse avoid using very hot water during routine handwashing with soap?

options.text: Hot water kills too many beneficial bacteria
Hot water strips protective skin lipids, increases dermatitis/chapping, and promotes bacterial colonization on damaged skin
Hot water inactivates plain soap completely
Hot water takes longer to rinse

questions.explanation: WHO recommends lukewarm or cool water because repeated exposure to hot water damages the stratum corneum, causing irritant contact dermatitis that harbors higher microbial counts and reduces compliance.
questions.hint: Think about how extreme water temperature affects skin barrier integrity over dozens of washes per shift.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: Which of the following statements about WHO Hand Hygiene standards are TRUE? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Alcohol-based hand rub is the preferred routine method when hands are not visibly soiled
Hands must be completely dry after applying ABHR before donning gloves
Paper towels used to dry hands should be reused for the next shift
The faucet handle (if non-sensor) should be turned off using a clean paper towel to avoid recontaminating clean hands

questions.explanation: ABHR is faster, more effective, and gentler than soap when hands are visibly clean; hands must dry completely before gloving to prevent irritation/glove perforation; non-sensor faucets must be turned off with a clean towel.
questions.hint: Evaluate each practice for preventing recontamination and maintaining skin/glove integrity.
questions.subject: Hand Hygiene (WHO Standard)

questions.question: What is the standard CDC/AIIMS sequence for DONNING (putting on) full Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?

options.text: Gloves -> Gown -> Mask -> Goggles
Gown -> Mask/Respirator -> Goggles/Face shield -> Gloves
Mask -> Gloves -> Gown -> Goggles
Goggles -> Gown -> Gloves -> Mask

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] After performing hand hygiene, the standard PPE donning sequence is: (1) Gown, (2) Mask or N95 Respirator, (3) Goggles or Face Shield, and (4) Gloves (pulled snugly over the gown cuffs).
questions.hint: Start by covering your body, then protect your airway and eyes, and finish with the item that touches the patient last.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: What is the standard CDC sequence for DOFFING (removing) full PPE to minimize self-contamination?

options.text: Mask -> Gown -> Goggles -> Gloves
Gown -> Mask -> Gloves -> Goggles
Gloves -> Goggles/Face shield -> Gown -> Mask/Respirator (followed by hand hygiene)
Goggles -> Gloves -> Mask -> Gown

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Doffing removes the most heavily contaminated item first: (1) Gloves, (2) Goggles/Face shield, (3) Gown, and (4) Mask/Respirator (removed outside the room for Airborne precautions), performing hand hygiene immediately after (and between steps if hands become contaminated). Note: Removing gown and gloves together in one roll is also an accepted CDC alternative.
questions.hint: Follow the principle of taking off the dirtiest item first and keeping respiratory protection on until the very end.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: While doffing PPE after caring for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis (Airborne precautions), WHERE should the nurse remove the N95 respirator?

options.text: Inside the patient's room right beside the bed
Outside the patient's room after closing the door
Inside the patient's bathroom
Before removing contaminated gloves

questions.explanation: For Airborne precautions, infectious droplet nuclei remain suspended inside the room. Therefore, gloves, eye protection, and gown are removed inside the room (near the doorway), while the N95 respirator is removed ONLY AFTER exiting and closing the door.
questions.hint: Think about where suspended airborne particles are still floating while you are undressing.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: When removing contaminated disposable gloves, which technique prevents transferring pathogens onto bare skin?

options.text: Pulling both gloves off by snapping them rapidly from the fingertips

Grasp the outside of the first glove near the wrist to peel it inside-out, hold it in the gloved hand, then slide ungloved fingers UNDER the cuff of the second glove to peel it inside-out over the first
Slide bare fingers over the outside palm of the second glove
Wash the gloved hands and pull them off by the fingers

questions.explanation: "Glove-to-glove, skin-to-skin" ensures contaminated outer surfaces only touch outer surfaces, and bare fingers touch only the clean inner surface of the second glove.
questions.hint: Remember the classic "glove-to-glove, skin-to-skin" removal rule.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: Immediately after donning an N95 particulate respirator, what must the nurse perform EVERY time before entering an airborne isolation room?

options.text: A full quantitative hospital fit-test with saccharin hood
A user seal check (positive and negative pressure check)
Spraying the outside of the mask with 70% alcohol
Pinching the nosepiece with one finger only

questions.explanation: Formal fit-testing is done annually (or when mask model/facial structure changes), whereas a user seal check (inhaling to verify slight collapse and exhaling to detect air leaks around the seal) must be performed EVERY time an N95 is donned.
questions.hint: Distinguish between the annual formal certification test and the quick bedside check done every single time you put on an N95.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: Which parts of a worn PPE set are considered "CLEAN" (safe to touch with bare hands during doffing)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The inside of the gloves
The inside of the gown and the back ties at the neck/waist
The head straps/ear loops of the mask and the headband/earpieces of goggles
The front chest panel of the gown and the front surface of the mask

questions.explanation: During doffing, the outside front of the gown, outside of gloves, front of mask, and front of goggles/shield are considered heavily contaminated. Only the inside surfaces and back ties/straps are treated as clean.
questions.hint: Separate the surfaces facing the patient from the surfaces touching the nurse's own body or behind the head.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: A nurse is putting on sterile gloves using the open-gloving technique for a urinary catheterization. Which part of the FIRST sterile glove may the nurse's bare non-dominant hand touch?

options.text: The outer palmar surface of the glove
The sterile fingertips of the glove
Only the folded-back inner cuff edge
Any part of the glove if hands were washed with soap

questions.explanation: In open sterile gloving, bare skin (clean, not sterile) may touch ONLY the inner surface of the folded cuff of the first glove. Then the sterile gloved fingers slip under the cuff of the second glove (sterile-to-sterile).
questions.hint: Apply the sterile-to-sterile and clean-to-clean boundary rule to the folded cuff.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: When donning disposable gloves over an isolation gown, how should the nurse position the glove cuffs?

options.text: Tuck the glove cuffs underneath the gown sleeves
Pull the glove cuffs up and snugly over the knitted cuffs of the isolation gown
Roll the gown sleeves up to the elbows before wearing gloves
Leave a 2-inch bare skin gap at the wrist for ventilation

questions.explanation: Extending the glove cuffs over the gown wrists creates a continuous protective barrier so blood or body fluids cannot seep onto the nurse's exposed wrist skin.
questions.hint: Think about how to eliminate any exposed skin gap at the wrist joint.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: A nurse is doffing a tie-back surgical mask. Which strap should be untied FIRST, and why?

options.text: Top strap first, so the mask drops onto the chest
Bottom strap first, then top strap, so the contaminated mask does not flop downward onto the nurse's uniform/neck
Both straps snapped simultaneously with gloved hands
Pull the front of the mask straight off the nose

questions.explanation: Untying the bottom tie first (while the top tie holds the mask in place) and then untying the top tie allows the nurse to lift the mask forward and away from the face without the contaminated front falling onto the uniform.
questions.hint: Visualize what happens by gravity if you untie the upper string while the lower string is still tied.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: A nurse has a full beard and is assigned to care for a patient with active measles. What is the safest respiratory PPE option for this nurse?

options.text: Wear a standard N95 respirator tightly over the beard
Wear two surgical masks layered together
Use a Powered Air-Purifying Respirator (PAPR) with a loose-fitting hood, or reassign care
Shave only the mustache and keep the beard

questions.explanation: Facial hair breaks the tight face-to-respirator seal required for an N95 mask to filter airborne particles. A loose-fitting PAPR hood does not rely on a tight facial seal and safely protects bearded staff.
questions.hint: Consider which airborne respiratory device provides positive airflow inside a hood without needing a tight cheek seal.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: During a surgical procedure, a scrub nurse notices a tiny puncture in their sterile glove. What is the nurse's immediate priority action?

options.text: Continue the procedure and wash hands afterward
Step back from the sterile field, notify the surgeon, perform hand hygiene if contaminated, and don a new pair of sterile gloves
Place a sterile adhesive bandage over the glove hole
Wipe the glove tear with povidone-iodine

questions.explanation: Any tear or puncture immediately compromises the sterile barrier and exposes both patient and nurse to contamination. The glove must be changed immediately using sterile technique.
questions.hint: Recall what happens to surgical asepsis the instant a barrier integrity breach occurs.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: Which action during PPE doffing requires IMMEDIATE hand hygiene BEFORE continuing to the next doffing step?

options.text: Touching the clean inside tie of the gown
Accidentally touching the contaminated front surface of the goggles or gown with bare hands
Stepping outside the door before removing the N95 mask
Looking in a mirror to check for self-contamination

questions.explanation: If hands become visibly or potentially contaminated at ANY point during doffing, the nurse must immediately stop and perform hand hygiene before touching the face, eyes, or clean mask straps.
questions.hint: Think of the safety pause required whenever bare skin contacts a dirty surface mid-doffing.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: When caring for a patient on Contact precautions ONLY (e.g., MRSA wound infection with no splashing risk), which PPE items are required upon entering the room?

options.text: N95 respirator and shoe covers
Isolation gown and clean disposable gloves
Surgical mask and face shield only
Sterile surgical gown and sterile gloves

questions.explanation: Contact precautions require a gown and gloves upon room entry to prevent direct/indirect transfer of pathogens from the patient or contaminated surfaces. Eye/mask protection is added only if splash/spray risk exists (Standard Precautions).
questions.hint: Identify the two core barrier items that block skin and clothing contact with contaminated surfaces.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Double-gloving is recommended during high-risk surgical procedures and orthopedic surgeries.
Reason (R): Wearing two pairs of gloves significantly reduces the risk of inner-glove perforation and bloodborne pathogen exposure to the healthcare worker's skin.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Evidence from CDC/WHO surgical safety guidelines confirms that double-gloving (often with a colored indicator inner glove) dramatically reduces inner-glove perforations and percutaneous blood exposure during high-risk surgeries.
questions.hint: Consider whether a second barrier layer protects the skin when sharp bone fragments or needles nick the outer layer.
questions.subject: PPE Donning & Doffing

questions.question: A flexible fiberoptic bronchoscope is classified under Spaulding's classification as a semi-critical item. Which chemical agent is most commonly used for its high-level disinfection?

options.text: 2% Alkaline Glutaraldehyde (Cidex)
70% Ethyl alcohol
0.5% Sodium hypochlorite
Chloroxylenol (Dettol)

questions.explanation: [NORCET-2 Shift-1 PYQ] Flexible bronchoscopes and endoscopes are heat-sensitive semi-critical items (contact mucous membranes). 2% alkaline glutaraldehyde (Cidex) provides high-level disinfection (20–45 minutes) without damaging delicate optics.
questions.hint: Recall the classic aldehyde-based high-level disinfectant used for heat-sensitive fiberoptic scopes.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: What are the standard temperature, pressure, and holding time parameters for routine moist-heat sterilization in a gravity-displacement autoclave?

options.text: 100 C at 5 psi for 10 minutes
121 C (250 F) at 15 psi for 15–20 minutes
160 C at 0 psi for 2 hours
63 C at 15 psi for 30 minutes

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Standard steam sterilization (autoclaving) operates at 121 C (250 F) under 15 lbs/sq inch (psi) pressure for 15–20 minutes (or 134 C at 30 psi for 3–4 minutes in prevacuum/flash cycles), killing all microbes including bacterial spores.
questions.hint: Match the classic moist-heat pressure-cooker settings: 15 psi and just above 120 degrees Celsius.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which biological indicator organism (spore test) is used to verify the sterilization efficacy of a steam autoclave?

options.text: Bacillus atrophaeus (formerly B. subtilis)
Geobacillus stearothermophilus
Staphylococcus aureus
Escherichia coli

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores are highly heat-resistant and serve as the gold-standard biological indicator for steam autoclaves and hydrogen peroxide plasma sterilizers. Bacillus atrophaeus is used for dry heat (hot air oven) and ETO gas.
questions.hint: Link the prefix "stearo-thermo-" (heat-loving) to steam sterilization testing.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: According to Spaulding's Classification, how are surgical forceps, urinary catheters, and cardiac catheters classified, and what level of processing do they require?

options.text: Critical items; require complete sterilization
Semi-critical items; require high-level disinfection
Non-critical items; require low-level disinfection
Semi-critical items; require soap and water cleaning only

questions.explanation: Critical items enter sterile body tissues, cavities, or the vascular system (surgical instruments, cardiac/urinary catheters, implants) and MUST be sterile.
questions.hint: Consider whether these instruments penetrate sterile tissues or merely touch intact skin.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which solution is recommended by hospital infection control guidelines for cleaning a large blood spillage (> 10 mL) on the Operation Theatre floor?

options.text: 70% Isopropyl alcohol
Sodium hypochlorite (1% or 0.5% available chlorine, freshly prepared)
2% Glutaraldehyde
Plain distilled water

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Sodium hypochlorite (0.5% to 1% available chlorine; typically 1% / 10,000 ppm for large blood spills after absorbing with absorbent granules/towels, with 10–20 min contact time) rapidly inactivates HBV, HCV, and HIV on environmental surfaces.
questions.hint: Think of the standard chlorine-based bleach disinfectant effective against bloodborne viruses on floors.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which sterilization method is BEST suited for heat-sensitive glass syringes, sharp stainless-steel scissors, liquid paraffin, and powders?

options.text: Steam autoclave
Hot air oven (Dry heat sterilization)
Boiling water
Pasteurization

questions.explanation: Dry heat (Hot air oven at 160 C for 2 hours or 170 C for 1 hour) sterilizes glassware, anhydrous oils, powders, and sharp metal instruments that would dull or rust in moist steam.
questions.hint: Choose the heat method that avoids moisture so oils, powders, and sharp edges are not ruined.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which gaseous chemical agent is widely used in CSSD to sterilize heat- and moisture-sensitive plastics, heart-lung machine components, and delicate catheters?

options.text: Ethylene Oxide (ETO) gas
Formaldehyde spray
Carbon dioxide gas
Nitrogen gas

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Ethylene Oxide (ETO) is an alkylating gas effective at low temperatures (37–55 C) for heat/moisture-sensitive plastics and electronics. Its major drawback is toxicity/flammability, requiring prolonged aeration (8–12 hours) before patient use.
questions.hint: Recall the low-temperature alkylating gas that requires a dedicated aeration cycle after sterilization.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: In a Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD), what is the correct unidirectional workflow of instruments from receipt to dispatch?

options.text: Sterile storage -> Packaging -> Decontamination -> Dispatch
Receiving/Decontamination (Dirty zone) -> Inspection & Packaging (Clean zone) -> Sterilization -> Sterile storage & Dispatch
Sterilization -> Decontamination -> Packaging -> Dispatch
Packaging -> Sterilization -> Decontamination -> Dispatch

questions.explanation: CSSD strictly enforces one-way (unidirectional) flow from Dirty (Decontamination, negative air pressure) -> Clean (Assembly/Packaging) -> Sterile (Sterilization & Sterile storage, positive air pressure) to prevent cross-contamination of sterile packs.
questions.hint: Follow the logical progression from soiled instruments arriving from wards to sterile packs leaving for OTs.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: What is the specific purpose of performing a daily Bowie-Dick test in a prevacuum steam autoclave?

options.text: To measure the pH of distilled water
To detect air leaks and verify adequate air removal and steam penetration in the chamber
To kill bacterial spores inside glass ampoules
To test the sharpness of surgical blades

questions.explanation: The Bowie-Dick test (Class 2 chemical indicator) is run daily in an empty prevacuum autoclave chamber to confirm that the vacuum pump effectively removes trapped air pockets, allowing uniform steam penetration.
questions.hint: Remember that trapped air prevents steam from reaching instruments—this daily test checks vacuum efficiency.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which of the following items are classified as NON-CRITICAL under Spaulding's Classification? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Blood pressure cuff
Stethoscope diaphragm
Bedpan and bedside rails
Endotracheal tube

questions.explanation: Non-critical items contact only intact skin (BP cuffs, stethoscopes, bedpans, rails) and require intermediate- or low-level disinfection. Endotracheal tubes contact respiratory mucous membranes and are semi-critical.
questions.hint: Pick the items that touch only intact outer skin rather than mucous membranes.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: After activating 2% alkaline glutaraldehyde (Cidex) by adding the activator powder, what is its typical maximum reuse shelf life (provided minimum effective concentration is verified)?

options.text: 24 hours
3 days
14 days (up to 28 days for certain extended-life formulations)
6 months

questions.explanation: Once activated, standard 2% alkaline glutaraldehyde remains active for 14 days (some newer formulations up to 28 days), and its minimum effective concentration (MEC >= 1.5–2%) must be checked daily with test strips.
questions.hint: Recall the classic two-week window after mixing the activator into standard Cidex.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: Which level of decontamination destroys ALL microorganisms EXCEPT high numbers of bacterial endospores?

options.text: Sterilization
High-level disinfection (HLD)
Low-level disinfection
Routine detergent cleaning

questions.explanation: Sterilization destroys ALL microbial life including bacterial spores. High-level disinfection (HLD) eliminates vegetative bacteria, mycobacteria, fungi, and viruses, leaving only small numbers of hardy bacterial spores.
questions.hint: Distinguish the process that kills everything including spores from the tier just below it.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: A nurse in the surgical ward checks a sterilized dressing pack before opening it and notices a small water stain on the paper-plastic pouch. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.text: Dry the pack under a warm lamp and use it
Treat the pack as contaminated (compromised sterility) and discard/return it to CSSD for reprocessing
Open it carefully and use only the gauze in the center
Check the expiration date and use it if within 30 days

questions.explanation: Under event-related sterility principles, moisture wicking through a porous wrapper ("strike-through") allows microorganisms to enter immediately, rendering the entire pack unsterile regardless of expiration date.
questions.hint: Recall the rule of "strike-through" moisture on sterile porous packaging.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: What is the primary difference between an "Antiseptic" and a "Disinfectant"?

options.text: Antiseptics kill spores while disinfectants do not
Antiseptics are formulated for safe application on living skin/tissues; disinfectants are formulated for inanimate objects/surfaces
Disinfectants are weaker than antiseptics
Antiseptics are used only in autoclaves

questions.explanation: Antiseptics (e.g., chlorhexidine, povidone-iodine, 70% alcohol on skin) inhibit/destroy microbes on living tissue, whereas disinfectants (e.g., sodium hypochlorite, glutaraldehyde, phenolics) are harsher chemicals used on inanimate surfaces and instruments.
questions.hint: Compare whether the chemical is intended for living tissue versus non-living surfaces.
questions.subject: Sterilization, Disinfection & CSSD

questions.question: According to India's Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules (2016 & 2018 Amendment), into which color-coded bag should a pus- or blood-soaked cotton swab and surgical wound dressing be discarded?

options.text: Yellow non-chlorinated plastic bag
Red non-chlorinated plastic bag
White translucent puncture-proof container
Blue cardboard box

questions.explanation: [NORCET-2 Shift-1 PYQ] Blood- or pus-soaked cotton swabs, bandages, dressings, and plaster casts are classified as "Soiled Waste" and must be segregated into the Yellow non-chlorinated plastic bag for incineration/plasma pyrolysis/deep burial.
questions.hint: Recall which color category handles anatomical and body-fluid-soaked soft dressings.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 (India), in which container should used IV tubing, urinary catheters, urine bags, and syringes WITHOUT needles be disposed?

options.text: Yellow bag
Red non-chlorinated plastic bag
White puncture-proof container
Blue cardboard box

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Contaminated recyclable plastic waste—including IV sets, tubing, IV bottles, catheters, uro-bags, gloves, and syringes without needles—goes into the Red non-chlorinated plastic bag for autoclaving/microwaving/hydroclaving followed by shredding and recycling.
questions.hint: Link "R" for Recyclable contaminated plastics to its matching color-coded bin.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Where should used hypodermic needles, scalpel blades, lancets, and syringes WITH fixed needles be discarded under India's BMW Rules 2016?

options.text: Yellow bag
Red bag
White translucent, puncture-proof, leak-proof, tamper-proof container
Blue cardboard box

questions.explanation: All metallic waste sharps—needles, blades, scalpels, lancets, and syringes with fixed needles—must be discarded into a White translucent puncture-proof, leak-proof, tamper-proof container to prevent needle-stick injuries.
questions.hint: Think of the rigid translucent container specifically designed to stop sharp metal tips from piercing through.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: According to India's BMW Management Rules 2016, broken glass ampoules, empty non-cytotoxic medicine vials, and metallic body implants are segregated into which color-coded container?

options.text: Yellow bag
Red bag
White translucent container
Puncture-proof and leak-proof cardboard box with Blue colored marking

questions.explanation: Contaminated glassware (broken/discarded glass, medicine vials, ampoules EXCEPT those contaminated with cytotoxic drugs) and metallic body implants go into a Blue-marked puncture-proof/leak-proof box for disinfection/autoclaving and recycling.
questions.hint: Recall the color reserved specifically for glassware (non-cytotoxic) and metallic orthopedic implants.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: A nurse finishes administering an IV chemotherapeutic (cytotoxic) agent such as cyclophosphamide. Where should the empty cytotoxic glass vial and contaminated IV tubing be discarded under India's BMW Rules 2016?

options.text: Yellow bag (labeled with cytotoxic hazard symbol)
Blue box for the glass vial and Red bag for the tubing
White puncture-proof container
Black general municipal waste bin

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Cytotoxic drugs and ALL items contaminated with cytotoxic drugs—including their glass vials, ampoules, syringes, and tubing—are an explicit exception to Blue/Red and MUST go into the Yellow bag for high-temperature incineration (>= 1200 C) or return to manufacturer.
questions.hint: Remember the strict safety exception where toxic chemotherapy waste overrides standard glass or plastic recycling bins.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Which of the following items belong in the YELLOW category under India's BMW Management Rules 2016 & 2018 Amendment? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Human anatomical waste (amputated limbs, placenta, biopsy tissue)
Expired or discarded antibiotic vials
Discarded blood bags and microbiology culture plates (after on-site pre-treatment)
Used nitrile examination gloves contaminated with urine

questions.explanation: Human/animal anatomical waste, soiled waste, expired/discarded medicines, chemical waste, blood-soaked linen, and pre-treated lab/blood bags go into Yellow. Contaminated recyclable gloves go into the Red bag.
questions.hint: Identify the biological, expired pharmaceutical, and lab/blood wastes while separating recyclable rubber/plastic gloves.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Under India's Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules 2016, what is the MAXIMUM permissible duration for storing untreated bio-medical waste on healthcare facility premises?

options.text: 12 hours
24 hours
48 hours
7 days

questions.explanation: [AIIMS NORCET PYQ] Untreated human anatomical waste, animal anatomical waste, soiled waste, and biotechnology waste must NOT be stored beyond 48 hours. If an emergency requires extending storage beyond 48 hours, written permission and steps to prevent environmental harm are mandatory.
questions.hint: Recall the exact two-day statutory ceiling for holding untreated infectious waste at a hospital.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Which major regulatory changes were introduced by the Bio-Medical Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2018 in India? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Phasing out chlorinated plastic bags (excluding blood bags) and gloves by March 27, 2019
Mandatory establishment of a bar-coding system for bags/containers containing BMW sent out of premises
Pre-treatment of laboratory waste, microbiological waste, blood samples, and blood bags on-site as per WHO Blue Book 2014 or NACO guidelines
Eliminating the White sharps container category completely

questions.explanation: The 2018 Amendment phased out chlorinated plastic bags (excluding blood bags) and gloves by March 27, 2019, mandated barcoding/GPS tracking for BMW bags, required on-site pre-treatment of lab/blood waste per WHO Blue Book 2014/NACO, and retained all four color categories.
questions.hint: Focus on the 2018 updates targeting chlorinated plastics, digital tracking, and on-site lab/blood pre-treatment.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Why did India's BMW Rules (2016 & 2018 Amendment) mandate phasing out CHLORINATED plastic bags (PVC) for biomedical waste collection?

options.text: Chlorinated bags are too expensive to print labels on
Burning chlorinated plastics during incineration releases toxic carcinogenic dioxins and furans
Chlorinated bags dissolve immediately in water
Chlorinated bags cannot be color-coded yellow or red

questions.explanation: Incinerating polyvinyl chloride (PVC / chlorinated plastics) generates persistent organic pollutants—specifically dioxins and furans—which are highly toxic carcinogens. Hence, non-chlorinated plastic bags are mandatory (with blood bags exempted in 2018).
questions.hint: Think about the dangerous toxic air pollutants created when chlorine-containing plastics are burned.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: According to India's BMW Rules 2016, how should an empty, uncontaminated paper wrapper from a sterile syringe and leftover patient food be segregated?

options.text: Yellow BMW bag
Red BMW bag
Blue BMW box
General solid waste bin (Black/Green municipal waste; not classified as BMW)

questions.explanation: Non-infectious general waste (paper wrappers, packaging, food scraps, office trash) is NOT bio-medical waste and must be segregated into municipal solid waste bins (commonly Black/Green/Blue municipal norms) to avoid inflating hazardous BMW volume.
questions.hint: Distinguish non-infectious everyday trash from regulated infectious hospital waste.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Under India's BMW Rules 2016, up to what fill level should a bio-medical waste bag or sharps container be filled before sealing and replacing?

options.text: 25% full (one-quarter)
50% full (halfway)
75% full (three-quarters)
100% full to the very brim

questions.explanation: BMW bags and sharps containers must never be overfilled; they should be securely tied/sealed and replaced once three-fourths (75%) full to prevent tearing, spillage, and needle-stick injuries.
questions.hint: Recall the three-quarters safety fill-line printed on hospital sharps bins and BMW bags.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Under India's Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules (2016 & 2018 Amendment), by what date must every healthcare facility submit its Annual BMW Report to the prescribed authority (State Pollution Control Board)?

options.text: January 31
March 31
June 30 every year
December 31

questions.explanation: Under Rule 13 of the BMW Management Rules 2016 (and 2018 Amendment), every occupier (healthcare facility) and CBWTF operator must submit an Annual Report on or before June 30 of every year for the preceding calendar year (Jan–Dec).
questions.hint: Remember the exact mid-year deadline at the end of June for submitting the previous year's report.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Under India's BMW Management Rules 2016, a hospital is prohibited from setting up its own on-site BMW incinerator if a Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF) is available within what distance?

options.text: 10 kilometers
25 kilometers
75 kilometers
200 kilometers

questions.explanation: Under Rule 7(3) of the BMW Management Rules 2016, no occupier shall establish an on-site treatment and disposal facility if a CBWTF service is available within a distance of 75 kilometers.
questions.hint: Recall the exact statutory radius (under 100 km) within which hospitals must use a centralized CBWTF.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)

questions.question: Which hazard symbol is universally printed on Yellow, Red, and White biomedical waste containers to alert handlers to infectious risk?

options.text: Radioactive trefoil symbol
Biohazard symbol (three interlocking crescents around a central circle)
Flammable flame symbol
High-voltage lightning symbol

questions.explanation: Schedule IV of India's BMW Rules 2016 mandates labeling infectious waste containers with the international Biohazard symbol (and the Cytotoxic hazard symbol "C" triangle specifically for cytotoxic drugs).
questions.hint: Identify the universal three-crescent warning emblem representing biological infection risk.
questions.subject: BMW Management (India Rules)
